text.p: Philippine wheat importers are likely to stay on the sidelines in the coming week, unless prices fall to interesting levels, traders said on Friday.
"We may just look at the market," said an executive in one of the country's largest flour millers.
Traders said they expected flour millers to book advance requirements only if prices fell to "very interesting levels."

"The U.S. markets at the moment do not reflect the world situation," said one trader. "Prices should come down some more in the U.S. markets to reflect the bumper harvests in other wheat producing regions in Europe, Australia, Argentina and
Philippine flour millers, who buy most of their wheat requirement from the U.S. markets, need some 70,000 tonnes of wheat for January.
Flour millers said they had ample wheat supply for November and December.
The Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing price of hard flour remained at 290 pesos per 25 kg bag, and soft flour at 260 pesos.
